hook_text: Look at the front of an ambulance. The word is back to front. It is not a mistake. It is written for a mirror.
clip_script: On the front of many ambulances, the word AMBULANCE is printed back to front. Why? Because a driver ahead sees it in a rear-view mirror, and mirrors swap left and right. Light obeys one simple law when it bounces: the angle it comes in at equals the angle it goes out at, both measured from a line at right angles to the mirror, the normal. Follow those bounces into your eye, trace them back in straight lines, and your brain places the image behind the glass: upright, the same size, as far behind as you are in front, but with left and right swapped. A still dam in the Drakensberg mirrors the mountains perfectly for the same reason. Let the wind ripple it, and the surface turns rough, the light scatters in every direction, and the picture vanishes.
visual_style: A whiteboard ambulance with reversed lettering, then a car mirror flipping it, then a ray diagram with the normal and equal angles, then a still dam with a perfect reflection breaking into sparkles.
pacing: A quick hook, a clear law, then a visual payoff.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw a reflection ray diagram.
